patterns.heroConsensus: Cinematic video or scroll-scrubbed drone reel, serif wordmark, transparent-to-solid nav. Christie's/Sotheby's lean editorial-still; The Agency/Kirman/Altman lean cinematic-video.
patterns.paletteConsensus: Deep navy OR true black as primary anchor + warm cream/ivory + metallic gold/champagne accent. Red is The Agency's ownable move (not recommended to copy).
patterns.typeConsensus: Editorial transitional serif display (Canela/Didot/Playfair) + clean geometric sans body (Inter/Neue Haas/Proxima).
patterns.navConsensus: Transparent fixed over hero that solidifies on scroll; serif wordmark left, minimal utility right.
patterns.ctaConsensus: Low-pressure, high-signal: 'Inquire', 'Private Showing', 'Meet [name]'. Never 'Contact Me' or 'Get a Free Quote'.

designRecommendations.bestReference: The Agency RE (theagencyre.com) — for cinematic execution and brand confidence; Christie's for editorial heritage anchoring. Blend: Christie's editorial gravitas + The Agency's cinematic scroll choreography.
designRecommendations.heroConcept: Scroll-driven drone cinematic over a Navesink River / Rumson waterfront estate at golden-twilight, with a secondary reveal of Pier Village boardwalk at dusk. Hero opens with a slow boom-out from a wood-shingle gable to a wide aerial crossing the river toward Sandy Hook. Christie's red + Carolina wordmark fades in on second beat. Scroll-scrubbed so the frame sequence advances as the user scrolls, ending locked on a Monmouth County skyline with the primary CTA 'Private Showing'.
designRecommendations.heroAnimation: GSAP ScrollTrigger-driven image-sequence playback (120-180 frames, AVIF), with parallax depth shift on foreground reeds and a subtle chromatic grade shift from cool-morning to warm-twilight across the scrub. Serif wordmark executes a 400ms weight-up reveal (regular to medium). Nav bar transitions transparent to deep-navy at 15% scroll. Subtle film-grain overlay at 4% opacity.
designRecommendations.colorPaletteRationale: Deep navy (#0B1F3A) honors Christie's heritage and reads as 'old-money Atlantic'. Shore sand + ivory cream evoke Monmouth's beach-town warmth without going tropical. Christie's Red (#9B2032) is a restrained brand tie-in used only for moments of emphasis (affiliation lockup, pullquotes, hover underlines). Champagne gold is the metallic accent for dividers, numerals, and key-figures. Seafoam is a single secondary accent reserved for Navesink/waterfront modules so the palette breathes.

typographyProposal.display: Fraunces (Google Fonts) — variable serif with optical-size axis; reads as Canela-adjacent editorial but modern and performant
typographyProposal.displayAlt: Cormorant Garamond as lighter alternate for pull-quotes
typographyProposal.body: Inter (Google Fonts) — clean neo-grotesque at 400/500 for body, 600 for UI
typographyProposal.mono: JetBrains Mono — used sparingly for MLS numbers and market-data stat blocks
typographyProposal.rationale: Fraunces delivers the Christie's/Sotheby's editorial-serif gravitas with the optical-size axis giving true display elegance at 80px+ while behaving well at body headings. Inter is the defensible modern body pairing used by Compass and every premium site of 2025-26. This pairing reads 'heritage Atlantic broker with a modern eye' — exactly Carolina's positioning.

sectionOrder: 1. Scroll-scrubbed cinematic hero (Navesink/Rumson drone + wordmark + primary CTA)
2. Christie's International Real Estate affiliation lockup (trust bar, understated)
3. Featured Properties (3-5 trophy listings, full-bleed hover-reveal cards, price-on-request)
4. Neighborhood Films — Holmdel, Red Bank, Rumson, Long Branch/Pier Village (scroll-pinned neighborhood storyteller)
5. Bilingual Carolina (Spanish/English) — editorial split-scroll bio with toggle; personal story + credentials
6. The Monmouth Portfolio (curated current + sold portfolio, not MLS grid)
7. Market Insights (quarterly Monmouth luxury market report; gated PDF download as lead magnet)
8. Client Stories (video or quote testimonials from past high-net-worth clients)
9. The Process (editorial treatment of the buying/selling concierge process)
10. Private Showing / Inquire (form + calendar; concierge framing, not 'Contact Me')
11. Footer with Christie's network, bilingual switch, offices, credentials
signatureInteractions: 1. Scroll-scrubbed drone hero sequence (GSAP ScrollTrigger + AVIF frame sequence): user literally pilots the drone over the Navesink as they scroll — signature moment.

2. Neighborhood Film scroll-pin: as user scrolls through Holmdel/Red Bank/Rumson/Long Branch, a pinned video panel cross-dissolves between neighborhoods with kinetic typography of median prices and lifestyle notes appearing in the margin.

3. Editorial split-scroll bilingual bio: left column holds a cinematic portrait of Carolina; right column scrolls through story chapters; user toggles EN/ES and text cross-fades with Spanish typography treated with equal editorial weight (not as an afterthought translation).
4. Hover-parallax trophy listings: featured property cards use a 3-layer parallax on hover (sky / architecture / foreground) with a micro-dolly feel — property appears to breathe.
5. Magnetic concierge CTA: the 'Private Showing' button has a magnetic cursor effect and a subtle gold underline-draw on approach; on-click opens an inline editorial form (not a modal blast).
antiPatterns: No Zillow/Realtor-style MLS firehose grids — curate, don't aggregate.
No stock photography of generic 'family with keys' or 'sold sign on lawn'.
No 'Contact Me' or 'Get a Free Home Valuation!' yellow CTA buttons.
No pop-up lead-capture blasts or chat widgets that slide in after 5 seconds.
No carousels with dots that auto-advance every 3 seconds (dated, feels 2015).
No drop shadows on cards, no rounded-2xl everything, no purple gradients — keep it editorial, not SaaS.
No emoji, no 'We sell dreams!' copy, no exclamation points in hero.
No generic 'About Me' page — it's a bilingual editorial bio or nothing.
No Comic/Lobster/script fonts anywhere. No Papyrus. No Montserrat-only (it's fine for body support, not display).
No tropical palette (turquoise/coral) — this is Atlantic old-money, not Miami.
No parallax everywhere — use it surgically on 2-3 moments so it feels intentional.
